notes: L1 oracle: universal-ctags 6.2.1 (tier B) through calibration/oracles/make/ctags_oracle.py, which corrects two verified defects of ctags' Make parser and counts them: 404 targets of backslash-continued statements moved from the statement's last physical line (where ctags reports every name) to the line that spells them, and 74 macros named private (a make modifier keyword, never a variable) dropped, all on jart/cosmopolitan. The harness's own uncorrected tier-B run of the same dialect reads sym_recall .9164 and sym_precision .9438 (L1 unmet; 292 of the 299 dialect-only definitions are those mis-lined names, 65 of the 359 oracle-only are the private macros)

L2 oracle: GNU Make 4.4.1 (tier A, built from the release tarball; macOS make 3.81 is refused by cosmopolitan's own Makefile) evaluating each Makefile-like file as an entry point under sandbox-exec, its prerequisite edges put back in the spelling the source uses (calibration/oracles/make/README.md). The truth is the literal-spelled pairs make confirmed: ref_recall is near 1 by construction, ref_precision is the informative number (23 of 1,488 pairs sit on lines make never evaluated in any configuration: 20 in valkey, 17 of them in src/unit/Makefile, 2 in cosmopolitan, 1 in prometheus). jart/cosmopolitan is also evaluated with MODE=x86_64, because its aarch64 branch is dead on the arm64 host

L2 scope: make's database holds 238,335 edges on cosmopolitan (default configuration), of which 51,820 sit under a spelled literal and 186,515 (78%) have a variable- or function-produced prerequisite that no static extractor sees; valkey 12,275 / 577 / 11,698, prometheus 128 / 40 / 88. The dialect emits only literal prerequisite words as references and claims none of the expanded edges; references spelled with a variable (a value, not a name) are not emitted

known extraction limits (LB-Q-makefile-rest): in a multi-target rule (a b: dep) the prerequisites are calls of the first target only (the engine attaches a call to the smallest callable that contains it and the targets share one range); the private and override modifiers of a target-specific assignment are read by the grammar as prerequisites, so their words are skipped and the targets are emitted; Makefile.common and docker.Makefile are not claimed (the manifest owns Makefile, makefile, GNUmakefile, *.mk and *.make, as the queue entry names)

per subject: jart/cosmopolitan sym 4,690 of 4,692 oracle definitions matched (157 files), prometheus/prometheus 56 of 56 (4 files), valkey-io/valkey 587 of 688 (.853; 16 files): its 101 misses are 73 tab-indented assignments inside conditionals (tree-sitter-make reads the line as a recipe of raw text, so no name node exists) and 28 unspaced VAR?=x forms (the grammar reads the ? into the name; VAR+=x is likewise read as the name VAR+ and skipped as the append it is)
